goals: Persist completed video recordings across browser sessions by storing them on the backend filesystem.
Allow users to organise recordings into named playlists.
Replace the ephemeral recording queue with a playlist-aware UI backed by the server.

userStories.title: Default playlist auto-created on first launch
userStories.description: As a creator, I want a default playlist to exist when I open the app for the first time so that I don't have to set anything up before my first recording is saved.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On `GET /api/playlists`, if no playlists exist on disk, the backend creates and returns a default playlist named `"My Playlist"` with a generated UUID.
The default playlist is persisted to `playlists.json` so it survives a server restart.
The frontend displays the default playlist name in the playlist header on load.
Typecheck / lint passes.
Visually verified in browser.

userStories.title: Completed recording auto-uploaded to active playlist
userStories.description: As a creator, I want each completed recording to be automatically uploaded and attached to the active playlist so that I never lose a generated video.

acceptanceCriteria.text: When a recording finalises in `use-recorder.ts`, the frontend immediately posts the MP4 blob to `POST /api/playlists/{id}/tracks` (where `{id}` is the active playlist ID).
The backend saves the file under `backend/recordings/{playlist_id}/{track_id}.mp4` and appends the track metadata (id, filename, created_at, size_bytes) to `playlists.json`.
The new track appears in the playlist UI without requiring a page reload.
Upload errors are surfaced as a visible error message to the user.
Typecheck / lint passes.
Visually verified in browser.

userStories.title: User can rename a playlist
userStories.description: As a creator, I want to rename a playlist so that I can give it a meaningful name (e.g. "Lofi Session March").

acceptanceCriteria.text: The playlist header shows the current playlist name with an edit affordance (e.g. inline editable field or pencil icon).
Submitting a new name sends `PATCH /api/playlists/{id}` with `{ "name": "..." }`.
The backend updates the name in `playlists.json` and returns the updated playlist.
The new name is reflected in the UI immediately and persists after a full page reload.
Typecheck / lint passes.
Visually verified in browser.

userStories.title: User can create a new playlist and switch between playlists
userStories.description: As a creator, I want to create additional playlists and switch between them so that I can organise recordings by project or session.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A "New Playlist" button sends `POST /api/playlists` with a default name (e.g. `"New Playlist"`), and the backend persists it and returns the new playlist object.
A playlist selector (dropdown or tab list) displays all existing playlists.
Selecting a playlist sets it as the active playlist; subsequent recordings are uploaded to it.
The active playlist's tracks are fetched from `GET /api/playlists/{id}/tracks` and displayed.
Typecheck / lint passes.
Visually verified in browser.

userStories.title: User can play, download, and delete tracks within a playlist
userStories.description: As a creator, I want to play, download, or delete any track in the active playlist so that I can manage my recordings.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each track row shows: filename, size (MB), created_at timestamp, and action buttons (Play, Download, Delete).
**Play:** clicking Play opens/plays the track video via a URL served by `GET /api/playlists/{playlist_id}/tracks/{track_id}/file`.
**Download:** clicking Download triggers a browser download of the MP4 file.

**Delete:** clicking Delete sends `DELETE /api/playlists/{playlist_id}/tracks/{track_id}`; the backend removes the file from disk and the entry from `playlists.json`; the track disappears from the UI immediately.
A confirmation dialog is shown before deleting a track.
Typecheck / lint passes.
Visually verified in browser.

functionalRequirements.description: ** Backend stores playlist metadata in `backend/playlists.json` — a JSON array of playlist objects, each with `id` (UUID), `name`, `created_at`, and a `tracks` array.
** Backend stores video files at `backend/recordings/{playlist_id}/{track_id}.mp4`; directories are created on demand.
** `GET /api/playlists` — returns all playlists (without track file bytes); creates default playlist if none exist.
** `POST /api/playlists` — creates a new playlist with a provided or default name; returns the created playlist object.
** `PATCH /api/playlists/{id}` — updates the playlist name; returns the updated object.
** `POST /api/playlists/{id}/tracks` — accepts `multipart/form-data` with the MP4 file; saves to disk; appends track metadata to `playlists.json`; returns the new track object.
** `GET /api/playlists/{id}/tracks/{track_id}/file` — streams the MP4 file from disk with correct `Content-Type: video/mp4` header.
** `DELETE /api/playlists/{id}/tracks/{track_id}` — removes the file from disk and the entry from `playlists.json`.
** Frontend replaces `recording-queue.tsx` with a new `playlist-panel.tsx` component that occupies the same position in the UI (below the audio player); it fetches and displays the active playlist.
** Frontend tracks `activePlaylitId` in React state; initialised to the first playlist returned by `GET /api/playlists` on app load.
** Backend layering: routes in `backend/routes/playlists.py`, service logic in `backend/services/playlist_service.py`, file I/O in `backend/repositories/playlist_repository.py`.
